items.statement: No new projects contributed to H1 FY26 revenue growth; growth driven by recovery in existing programs and base effect.
items.quote: So, there is absolutely no new project which has contributed to being revenue growth. BMW cars prototyping is happening somewhere. The pickup is good there. Second many for existing projects which were earlier, you know in last year our plan was to grow 25 -30%.

items.statement: Aims to sustain or exceed 15% revenue CAGR and grow faster than the market over the medium to long term
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aim to sustain if not exceed this momentum and continue to grow faster than the overall market that is a key direction that we are going in and this will be driven by a couple of factors first, we want to realise the full potential of our existing network.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA to grow faster than the historical 18% CAGR driven by operational efficiencies and operating leverage
items.quote: And we expect our EBITDA to grow at a faster pace than this historical CAG R and which will be driven by a couple of measures again

items.statement: Targets at least 20% plus ROCE over the next five years
items.quote: So overall, I feel we expect a trend of at least a 20% plus ROCE over the next five years.

items.statement: Expects corporate EBITDA margin to reach 21%-22% in near term and 27%-28% pre-corporate cost in long term (4-5 years)
items.quote: We are at 19% in Q2. We have delivered an EBITDA margin of 19% in Q2. And as I had said, based on our higher-than-market revenue growth and operating leverage, we expect the margins to grow faster than the historical trend. Obviously, it is upwards of 21%, 22%.

items.statement: Expects 4%-5% annual realisation improvement and 9%-10% volume growth in near to midterm
items.quote: Overall, we are looking at 4% to 5% reali sation improvement every year. And the volume growth will be in the region of 9% to 10

items.statement: Targets revenue potential of 100% (from current 56%) in 4-5 years at existing price points
items.quote: It is practical and doable because we have taken optimal occupancy and utilisation. We have not taken 100% occupancy and 100% utili sation. These are practically doable revenue numbers at existing price points

items.statement: Plans Rs.600-700 crore capex over next 2-3 years, including Rs.300 crore maintenance capex
items.quote: So in the next two to three years, it is about Rs. 600 crore to Rs.700 crore, out of which about Rs.300 crore will be maintenance capex.

items.statement: Maintenance capex expected at Rs.90-100 crore annually; expansion capex Rs.500-600 crore over 2-3 years
items.value: Rs.90 crore to Rs.100 crore annually
items.quote: Now, as the size of the network has grown, we expect maintenance capex to be in the range of Rs.90 crore to Rs.100 crore annually. In addition, we would like to spend additional Rs.500 crore to Rs.600 crore over the next two, three years to fund expansion.

items.statement: Plans 1,000 bed addition: ~700 beds brownfield (Ahmedabad, Vizag, Baroda, Cuttack) and 200-400 beds greenfield (Pune, Surat, Varanasi, Kanpur)
items.quote: I think brownfield will add about 700 beds through that route. And in markets like Ahmedabad, Vizag, Baroda, Cuttack, so that is our brownfield expansion plan. And as far as greenfield expansion is concerned, in newer cities like Pune, Surat, Varanasi, Kanpur, to name a few, while it is just indicative, we have identified 10 to 12 cities in that bucket, that will be about 200 to 400 beds.

items.statement: Incremental revenue split: 70-75% from existing centres, 10-15% brownfield, 8-10% greenfield over 4-5 years
items.quote: Our big part of our incremental revenue, about 70% -75% of our incremental revenue is going to come from existing centres, right? 10%-15% is going to come from brownfield expansion, and about 8%-10% is going to come from the greenfield expansion that we have, planned for.

items.statement: Mature centres (>Rs.10 crore/month) deliver 25% EBITDA pre-corporate cost and 27% pre-corporate ROCE
items.quote: Our mature centres doing more than Rs.10 crore of revenue are already delivering an EBITDA of 25% pre corporate cost. So as more and more centres come into this bucket, our EBITDA margins would grow at a healthy CAGR.

items.statement: Procurement identified as a lever to improve margins
items.quote: That is right. Procurement is going to be also one of the levers that we are going to work on to improve margins.

items.statement: Undertaking annual pricing benchmarking exercise across markets; results expected in couple of weeks
items.quote: From time to time, we undertake an exercise to understand where we are, in terms of pricing vis-à-vis our competitors, and currently also we have undertaken that exercise which should get over in the next couple of weeks.

items.statement: Revenue split: Radiation 20%, Medical Oncology 42%, balance Diagnostics and Surgical
items.quote: As far as your question on the split is concerned, radiation is today 20% of our overall revenue, medical is about 42%, and the balance is driven by diagnostics and surgeries, surgical.

items.statement: Institutional payor mix 34% in FY2025; CGHS is 12%-13% of institutional business
items.quote: In that institutional business, CGHS is in the range of 12% to 13% from the institutional business.

items.statement: Claims superior clinical outcomes vs multi-specialty hospitals; sees volume shift to single-specialty centres as awareness rises
items.quote: Cancer is a very complex disease to handle and it requires a super-speciality focus, which we have delivered and shown that clinical outcomes that we deliver are far superior to multi-speciality hospitals.

items.statement: Added senior leaders: Head of Clinical Strategy, CMO, CIO, Heads of International and Domestic Sales
items.quote: We have added some new roles in the team and we have on-boarded some senior leaders, from a reputed organization in the sector into the team. As I said, and I want to just reiterate that, roles like Head of Clinical Strategy to drive focus on identifying good clinical talent, good oncologists across our network and on-board them.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA at 2.5x; targets maintaining 2-2.5x pre-Ind AS; capex funded via internal accruals and borrowing headroom
items.quote: Net debt to EBITDA ratio is two-and-a-half times today and we are comfortable with that right now. And a lot of this capex funding is going to come from internal accruals, because we are mindful of this leverage ratio.

items.statement: Evaluating equity-debt ratio; will take appropriate call at appropriate time
items.quote: So, we are evaluating our equity and debt ratio. And at an appropriate time, we will take an appropriate call on that.

items.statement: Evaluating strategic options for Milann vertical, including potential divestment
items.quote: I think one of the options, while we are still evaluating, just to be very clear, could be divestment of this vertical. But again, not a definitive answer at this point in time, because we are evaluating various options.

items.statement: Mature centre vintage 10+ years; mid bucket 6-7 years; smaller centres <5 years or limited by size
items.quote: The bucket which has centres doing more than Rs.10 crore per month are about 10 years plus vintage and the middle bucket that I mentioned are about six to seven years.

items.statement: Mature centre growth trajectory: 1x asset turnover, 15-20% EBITDA margin, 15-20% ROCE in 4-5 years
items.quote: 1x asset turnover in four to five years and that is the typical growth trajectory we take. Also a 15% to 20% EBITDA margin in the same time period and 15% to 20% ROCE in the same time period.

items.statement: Refrains from centre-level guidance; adopts cluster-based approach; some centres require turnaround via clinical talent, programs, infrastructure
items.quote: We want to refrain from giving centre-wise guidance today. We are looking at a cluster-based approach to our business. And all the clusters have done well in the past. However, to answer this question specifically, there have been concerns in the past about some of our centres.

items.statement: Doctor incentive model primarily fixed retainer; fee-for-service in some markets (e.g., Western cluster); no plan to change
items.quote: I think many of our doctors are on a retainer fixed model. And I think that is the preferred model that we have in our system, people who are full timers with us. But of course, different markets have different nuances, like the Western cluster, many of the doctors prefer to be on a fee for service model.

items.statement: Smart metering revenue expected ~INR500 cr in H1 FY26 and ~INR300 cr in H2 FY26
items.quote: Revenues will be of the order of about INR500-odd crores in the first half. Exact number, I'm not able to disclose that to you. And then, of course, in the second half, we also plan some execution, which will be of the nature of about INR300-odd crores.

items.statement: OSAT commercial production started with sample shipments; focus on customer approvals for FY27 revenue ramp
items.quote: So, this year, while we did put a small target on us for revenues, but I'm not very sure whether we'll be pursuing the target more than pursuing approval from these three customers, because the approval from these three customers will help us to do good reven ues, starting from FY '27

items.statement: OSAT balance capex INR10.3 bn funded via QIP, internal accruals, transitory debt; PCB capex INR14 bn with INR3.2 bn balance funded via QIP, internal accruals, debt and INR3 bn central subsidy
items.value: INR10.3 bn OSAT; INR14 bn PCB
items.quote: First balance requirement for OSAT INR10.3 billion will be funded through QIP and spent amount of about 3.8 billion and balance internal accruals capex spread over five years and some transitory debt. Second thing is that with regard to PCB, the current plan includes only capex of 14 billion for which the balance requirement is 3.2 billion and up central government subsidy of about 3 billion.

items.statement: Net working capital cycle (ICAI guideline) 87 days in FY25 vs 83 days in FY24; initiatives include supply chain finance, factoring, bill discounting, inventory optimization
items.quote: the net working capital cycle inventory days plus receivable minus payable days calculated as per ICAI guideline. Note that guidance note is 87 days in F Y '25, up from 83 days in FY '24, increase of four days year-on-year

items.statement: Smart meter receivables INR687 cr as of Sep FY26 including non-current portion; ~INR240 cr to be discounted off books; target collection within 90 days
items.quote: As of September, I think the total receivables is about – yes, of the total receivables, about INR687 crores pertains to business of smart meters, which includes also the other non-current assets portion. So, we are quite confident that INR240 crores, approximately INR240 crores of such receivables will anyway get discounted and it'll reduce the amount.

items.statement: H2 FY25 smart metering net margin 9% (INR5,327 mn revenue, INR489 mn PAT); H1 FY25 loss driven by low revenue INR851 mn, fixed costs, due diligence provisions, corporate cleanup
items.quote: Now the H2 FY '25 net margin is only 9% actually, the revenues of INR5,327 million and PAT of INR489 million. So the 28% margin cited appears incorrect.

items.statement: Strong growth in automotive, industrial, EVs, railways, aerospace/defense, IT; non-smart meter verticals growing faster than company average
items.quote: As far as the other verticals are concerned, there is strong growth in automotive, there is strong growth in industrial other than smart meters, there is strong growth in electric vehicles. Also, now the resurgence of strong sectors like railways, electronics, as well as aerospace, outer space and defense, and also in IT field.

items.statement: Smart meter share of total business trending down; new non-AMISP device orders from multiple customers; exiting AMISP model to become pure device manufacturer
items.quote: We are also planning to exit from day one. When we took over this company, we wanted only to become a device manufacturer. So, we will no longer be an AMISP company. We will be only device company to various AMISPs.

items.statement: Interest cost ~10% including bill discounting; OSAT and PCB capex funded via QIP, internal accruals, transitory debt; no reliance on parent for OSAT funding
items.quote: Further, while calculating interest cost on the average borrowings, we need to consider bill discounting. The interest cost will work out approximately 10% including all bills discounted.

items.statement: Central government OSAT subsidies received within one week of approval; dedicated subsidy management team formed; DPR capex suppliers provide credit terms
items.quote: Whatever little we have spent, and wherever there was dues from the government have been fulfilled within one week's time. Like, for instance, we got the land related discount subsidies within one week of approval from the central government.

items.statement: Bad debt provision 3.5% of sales in H1 per ECL policy; provisions not write-offs; custom-built business limits actual write-offs; collections continue post-provision
items.quote: A bad debt provision does not mean it's a bad debt written off. It's a provision for write off as per the accounting policies and the ECL that we discover. And then obviously, it's also advised by the auditors.

items.statement: Added leadership in taxation, finance, manufacturing; strengthening internal controls, audit processes, disclosure checks; ERP-driven data flow to minimize manual intervention
items.quote: Regarding structural improvement, we have added more people on the taxation side, more people on finance, manufacturing, and brought more leadership into the company. And we are committed. We'll also re-examine, revisit our structural as well as communication models.

items.statement: Only one minor error: omitted related party disclosure in subsidiary notes; accounting correct; implementing software for contra-entry automation to prevent recurrence
items.quote: So, some total of this is that factually speaking, there is only one small error of not mentioning in the notes to accounts of a disclosure of a related party transaction, which you've taken note of and we'll make sure that in future, such misses don't happen.

items.statement: Iskraemeco acquisition: INR1,150 mn customer contract intangible recognized; net capital reserve adjustment; Sensonic acquisition: goodwill recognized; both netted in consolidation per Ind AS 103
items.quote: As far as the acquisition of Iskraemeco is concerned, the identified intangible asset customer contract was an amount of INR115 crores or INR1,150 million, which is recognized under the block technical know-how as a significant factor for design, implementation know-how, hosting, and communication package for smart meter.

items.statement: Bill discounting cost embedded in smart metering contract pricing; discounting done judiciously based on cost-benefit; foreign bank rates lower than domestic
items.quote: Discounting cost in the long term, smart metering receivables is already embedded in the contract pricing and bill discounting is undertaken judiciously based on the cost benefit assessment.

items.statement: OSAT facility: three anchor clients (Alpha Omega, Infineon, L&T-Fujitsu); samples shipped; commercial production technically started; awaiting full customer qualifications
items.quote: We have acquired three clients. They all of them have themselves come out and given press statements, actually, because we are not allowed to talk about it unless we get consent. But they have, so these are Alpha Omega Semiconductor, Infineon, and the Larsen and Toubro's business takeover of one portion of Fujitsu General's Semiconductor business.

items.statement: R&D capitalization policy: experimental research expensed; product development with revenue stream capitalized; amortization starts at revenue cycle; Kavach program developed with German tech
items.quote: Only when we identify a particular product with a revenue stream possibility, we take it as development and that is capitalized. And until the time when we start the revenue cycle, the moment revenue cycle comes, then amortization will start.

items.statement: Contingent liability INR5.2 bn (18% net worth) vs INR2.7 bn (11%) in FY24; driven by INR1.9 bn performance bank guarantees for Iskraemeco projects and INR1.3 bn corporate guarantees to subsidiaries
items.quote: the key increases relate to 1.9 billion of performance bank guarantees issued to Iskraemeco projects. Then 1.3 billion of corporate guarantees issued to subsidiary companies, K aynes Electronics Manufacturing Private Limited, INR1.2 billion and Iskraemeco 0.1 billion

items.statement: Railway expanded from signaling to rolling stock and Kavach; aerospace/defense orders growing; ODM solutions core to EMS growth for next 4-5 years
items.quote: Earlier, we were only in signaling in railway. Today, we have got into rolling stock. Then Kavach, we have added. So, our main concentration will never move out from EMS, and we are committed to that.

items.statement: First in India to ship OSAT chipsets despite latest approvals; three global semiconductor clients secured; technical capabilities differentiating
items.quote: One of them, we were the first in the country to actually ship out the chipsets, even though we got this thing the last, the approvals the last. And so, the samples have been shipped out, so in some sense, technically, the commercial production has started.

items.statement: Aerospace orders from foreign OEM; OSAT clients include global semiconductor majors (Alpha Omega, Infineon); export revenue share not quantified
items.quote: And then, of course, the last one is aerospace, which we have acquired a sizable amount of orders from one of the OEMs abroad. And this is increasing also from their own statements in the media.

items.statement: Cash flow statement purchase of fixed assets INR9.5 bn includes INR7.8 bn PPE/CWIP/intangibles, INR1.7 bn ROU assets net of subsidy; reconciles with asset additions
items.quote: The purchase of fixed assets in the cash flow statements amounting to 9.5 billion includes 7.8 billion of PPE, CWIP, Capital WIP that is, intangibles after adjusting for capital advances and payable of capital goods. INR1.7 billion of right of use assets, ROU assets, net of subsidy.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue growth > H1 FY26, H2 FY26 revenue > H1 FY26
items.quote: in H2, the revenue will be more than H1. That is what I can give you guidance

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin >20%, Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin ~15%
items.quote: Quarter 3 is the company's highest top line and highest EBITDA margin quarter. And in quarter 3, upwards of 20% EBITDA, which we have done in quarter 2, a number of 15% EBITDA.

items.statement: FY27 offline EBITDA profitability, FY28 offline PAT profitability
items.quote: FY '27 will be EBITDA level profitable in our complete offline. And FY '28 will go to PAT or something.

items.statement: 3-5 year revenue and profitability growth, TAM-driven
items.quote: We want to grow sustainably, both revenue improvement as well as profitability improvement. Both numbers will you see in the next 3-5 years, because the TAM is huge.

items.statement: Offline revenue growth ~25%-30% sustainable
items.quote: The growth of offline will be sustainable, and that will be ~25%-30%.

items.statement: Online ACPU growth ~8% YoY, FY26 full-year ACPU in same region
items.quote: We saw an ~8% increase in our online ACPU and we feel that our academic cycle, depending on how the enrollments come in, we expect the full year number to be in the same region.

items.statement: Offline center profitability: Year 1: -5% EBITDA, Year 2: +6% EBITDA, Year 3: +13%-15% EBITDA
items.quote: In the first year, it's minus ~5%, in the second year it's plus ~6% and in the third year, it's plus ~13% IGAAP EBITDA.

items.statement: Offline Vidyapeeth centers: 72/117 profitable (pre-Ind AS)
items.quote: ~72 out of 117 centers of our Vidyapeeth, which is JEE, NEET offline are profitable.

items.statement: Offline online admissions: ~80% of offline admissions from online
items.quote: ~80% of our offline admissions happen through online.

items.statement: Offline teacher cost: FTP (Faculty Training Program) mix rising to ~35%
items.quote: This will go to next year ~35%.

items.statement: Offline student-teacher ratio: Year 1: ~68-69, Year 2: ~75, Year 3: ~82-90
items.quote: In our first year, the student-teacher ratio goes to ~68-69, then the next year it goes to ~75, then it goes to ~82, then it goes to ~90s.

items.statement: Online-offline margins: Online ~35%-45% EBITDA, Offline ~13%-15% EBITDA (steady state)
items.quote: Steady state margins of online business is somewhere between ~35% to ~45% EBITDA and steady state margins for our offline business is ~13% - ~15% EBITDA.

items.statement: Marketing spend: H1 FY26 ~10%, FY26 ~8%-9% (vs ~9.6% FY25)
items.quote: Overall in H1, it is around ~10%. In the whole year, this number is going to be ~8%-9%.

items.statement: Offline center profitability delayed by short-term course ARPU impact
items.quote: In the first half, no picture or color comes out. Entire picture will come out on an annual year basis and not half-yearly basis.

items.statement: Acquired 53.33% controlling stake in CrudeChem Technologies Group (four US entities) for ~$11.5M; combined annual revenue $68M; EPS-accretive; 25-30% of consideration as primary capital infusion
items.quote: Fineotex through its subsidiary has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire equity interest in four U.S.-based specialty chemical companies forming the CCT Technologies Group, the CrudeChem Technologies Group ecosystem, with a combined annual revenue of USD 68 million. Across these entities, Fineotex will acquire 53.33% controlling stake with a combined acquisition value of approximately $1

items.statement: CCT capacity insufficient for lined-up orders; moving to larger premises in weeks; Fineotex India has spare capacity from newly commissioned plant
items.quote: when it comes to CrudeChem, we have to expand very quickly here because the area and speed of the businesses an d the kind of orders which are lined up is not able to handle in the same facilities. So by in the coming week or this week or something, there is another, we are going to finalize to shift in a couple of months to a new premises

items.statement: Fineotex will provide working capital support to CCT; enable consignment-based business, better raw material pricing, attract more orders
items.quote: support on the working capital and investments in the growth as going to be a good bargaining power to procure the raw materials at a lower price, support the customers for longer consignment-based businesses, attract some more orders on that line

items.statement: CCT is debt-free; Fineotex has Rs 300+ cr cash (Rs ~340 cr as of Sep); no debt raise needed; all investments from internal accruals
items.quote: We have more than Rs. 300 crores plus in cash and bank at the moment, not at the moment, I mean, in a couple of quarters before, I mean, in the September results also, it must be around 340 if I'm not wrong. So yes, that is sufficient enough to cater and we will not have to go to raise any debt for the requirement of working capital or investments to be done in CrudeChem.

items.statement: Three CCT founders (industry veterans, one PhD) remain as partners/shareholders; no exits; will collectively run business with Fineotex
items.quote: No, they are still the partners. Nobody's exiting out. We have acquired from each of them and equally. And also we have acquired, the company has also issued the shares. So it's something like that. So all of them will still be there.

items.statement: North American oilfield chemicals market $11.5B opportunity in 2025; strong growth across production, stimulation, water treatment segments
items.quote: The North American oilfield chemicals market alone represents a $11.5 billion opportunity in 2025, strong growth expected across refining midstream production chemicals and water treatment.

items.statement: No further fundraising required; Rs 300+ cr cash sufficient for CCT investments and working capital; geared for more acquisitions
items.quote: So yes, that is sufficient enough to cater and we will not have to go to raise any debt for the requirement of working capital or investments to be done in CrudeChem. So that's about it. So everything will be done with internal accruals and cash on bank, and it's much, much sufficient. And in fact, we are geared for more further investments in CCT or anything like that.

items.statement: Complementary portfolios across production, stimulation, water treatment; Fineotex formulation chemistry + CCT R&D enables co-development, faster innovation, end-to-end solutions
items.quote: The complementary product portfolio of Finotex and CrudeChem creates strong opportunities for cross -selling high-value solutions across both customer bases, enabling us to expand our reach in India, Asia and North America. CrudeChem's robust R&D infrastructure in Texas, combined with Fin eotex expertise in formulation chemistry will accelerate technology transfers, co -developments for advanced c

items.statement: Revenue growth expected to improve in absolute terms due to cell availability
items.quote: In absolute terms, it will improve as it is, but in the market, there are many situations, many parameters, many situations. We believe it should improve, but with the industry, with the whole industry.

items.statement: Capex of INR 350-400 crore for Dadri solar cell line
items.quote: In Dadri our budget was approximately around INR 350 to 400 crores and we assume we will, like better project execution and with better numbers we are trying to close it.

items.statement: Sales deferred due to GST rate cut from 12% to 5% on solar equipment
items.quote: The decline in revenue was largely due to the impact of the GST rate cut on solar equipment from 12% to 5%. The announcement and implementation of this change created a temporary pause in the market as customers postponed purchases to benefit from the lower tax rate.

items.statement: Partial recovery of deferred sales expected, but not full
items.quote: So definitely some of it will be recovered but not as much as the loss that has happened 1n that period. What happens is that the sale that is lost, is lost

items.statement: Material margin improvement due to in-house manufacturing of panels and batteries
items.quote: A key driver for this margin improvement was the movement in material margin, which improved by 0.7% over last year. This came mainly from higher in-house manufacturing across solar panels and batteries.

items.statement: Material margin improvement of 1% over last year for H1 FY26
items.quote: Material margin improved by 1% over last year, supported by the expansion in in-house panel and battery manufacturing capacities and the benefit of scale.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve due to AI adoption in sales network
items.quote: We have been working on AI for 3 years. And through AI, we are able to improve our conversion ratio. And we expect that in the coming time, our operational margin will improve due to AI.

items.statement: Demand driven by awareness of energy savings and unreliable grid
items.quote: growth of the company has come due to awareness. As soon as the Prime Minister Surya Ghar Muft Biyli Yojana came, due to its awareness, our market share of off-grid also increased a lot. I mean, market share did not increase, the market increased. Basically, that's because of awareness

items.statement: Government schemes like PM Surya Ghar Muft Biyli Yojana boosting demand
items.quote: India's push towards rooftop solar adoption and rising household awareness of energy saving are expanding the addressable market.

items.statement: Sales recovery in December due to improved DCR cell availability
items.quote: This month we have been able to sell. If you see the previous month and the month prior, we weren’t able to sell. This month we have been able to sell.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Panels (45%), Batteries (20%), Electronics (28%), Others (6%)
items.quote: Out of INR 11,652 million, INR 5,290 million belongs to panel, which comes to nearly 45%. Battery comes to INR 2,374 million. And all the electronics comes nearly around, it will be INR 3,300 million, which comes to your 28%.

items.statement: Megawatt execution: Panels (302 MW), Batteries (481 MW), Electronics (640 MW)
items.quote: We sold panels of 302 megawatt and battery 481 megawatt and electronics close to 640 megawatts.

items.statement: Temporary inventory increase due to sales deferral and backward integration
items.quote: The increase in the inventory in this quarter is due to as Pawan sir explained about the sale deferrals that was there. So, we ordered few inventories in the past, as we need to maintain our inventory level but due to these sales deferrals our inventory has slightly gone up and our inventory days has gone to 108 days.

items.statement: Inventory days expected to stabilize at 90-98 days post-backward integration
items.quote: At least sir, it will be, historically, it was around to 90 to 98 days, so we believe it will be somewhere around that.

items.statement: INR 2,750 crore used for debt repayment post-IPO
items.quote: Post-IPO, we have utilized INR 2,750 million for debt repayment.

items.statement: Mobility revenue expected to grow double-digit over next couple of years with margin expansion
items.quote: So yes, we will see significant growth in the next couple of years. Definitely double-digit going forward, and it also should contribute to the margin expansion going forward.

items.statement: Mobility loco contract delivery schedule: 40 units for 2 years, then 80 for 2 years, then 100 for 2 years, then 160 for remainder
items.quote: The contract requirements are 40 to be delivered for the next two years, which then gets stepped up to 80 for two years, which then gets stepped up to 100 for two years, which then gets stepped up to 160 for the rest.

items.statement: Mobility margin at 7.7% in FY25, up 50 bps YoY; expects margin expansion from loco project ramp-up
items.quote: We have reached 2.6 billion in fiscal year '25, which means the profitability went up by 23% and reached a margin of 7.7%, which is an improvement of 50 basis points versus prior year.

items.statement: DI margin range guided at 6%-8% for future, driven by transfer pricing; service growth could improve margins
items.quote: I told you that the more or less the margin range we expect is 6%-8% plus/minus, where we are right now and where we also will be in the future.

items.statement: Private CapEx outlook positive in medium term (April-June) due to tax cuts, GST reduction, PLI; very positive 2-3 years out with FTA resolution
items.quote: So, in the medium term, I am optimistic. I believe by April to June we should start , logically, with everything the 25 government has done. You have got a PLI in place, you have got a reduced income tax in place, you have got a reduced GST in place

items.statement: Ongoing CapEx: Medium Voltage GIS and Vacuum Interrupters; commercial production starts Oct '26 for MV, couple months earlier for Vacuum Interrupters
items.quote: So, the ongoing CapEx is basically the Medium Voltage, GIS Medium Voltage , and the Vacuum Interrupters. I think we will start commercial production in October ’26 on the 37 Medium Voltage and a couple of months earlier , plus/minus couple of months , on the Vacuum Interrupters

items.statement: Aurangabad bogie factory completed; evaluating whether to expand in-house or partner for further localization
items.quote: So, Aurangabad is bogies, we have done it already. And we are looking now how we need to do that. We are even considering whether it really makes sense to do it ourselves, do we work with partners instead, how much to localize.

items.statement: Working capital investment increased for Mobility 9K HP loco ramp-up; majority done, cashflows to stabilize and improve in full fiscal year
items.quote: Honestly, no. This was just more or less related to the ramp up of the 9K horsepower project and also some other larger projects. So, I would expect right now the majority is done, so it will stabilize.

items.statement: QCO norms impacted Low Voltage business for one quarter (Q1); now fully compliant, QCO lifted indefinitely; continuing localization regardless

items.statement: Current organic mix: ~35% turnkey ASIC, ~65% services, 0% ASSP; target FY27 mix with Kinetic: 50-55% ASSP, 30% turnkey ASIC, 15% services
items.quote: At the end of FY 27, the revenue mix should be that the ASSP business, which is the third business, the custom product IP business, thanks to Kinetic will be almost 50% of our business, or 50% to 55%.

items.statement: Kinetic top 10 customers account for ~40% of revenue; 60% of business goes through distribution
items.quote: So, the top 10 customers probably account for like 40% of the total revenue. 60% of the business really goes through distribution, which is pretty normal course in the semiconductor business for these customers.

items.statement: Partnerships with GlobalFoundries for wafer supply, Amkor for assembly/packaging, Navitas for GaN, Anora for test/validation to secure cost structure and differentiation
items.quote: You need a foundry partner that provides reliable supply and favorable pricing because the wafer alone accounts for up to 60% of the cost. That is why our partnership with Global Foundries is very important.

items.statement: Won SCL fab execution project for 180nm process upgrade in Mohali demonstrating ability to orchestrate complex multi-partner semiconductor programs
items.quote: A clear proof of our high-end service offering is our win to execute the SCL fab in Mohali for a 180-nanometer process upgrade, a complex multi-partner program that demonstrates our ability to orchestrate ecosystems, integrate global technology partners, and deliver large-scale, mission-critical semiconductor programs.

items.statement: Custom ASIC demand growing 3x faster than standard products; market structurally underserved for mid-tier customers needing high integration and low volume production
items.quote: Demand for custom chips is growing three times faster than standard products, yet the market remains structurally underserved, and mid-tier customers are left without dependable partners for higher levels of integration and low volume production.

items.statement: Power semiconductors represent largest analog/mixed signal market with $40B+ TAM, most disrupted by AI-driven electricity demand
items.quote: In fact, power semiconductors are the largest analog and mixed signal market with over a $40 billion TAM, and it's most disrupted because of AI.

items.statement: Adequate cash to fund Kinetic acquisition immediately; will evaluate debt instruments to optimize shareholder value
items.quote: Firstly, as you know, we have adequate cash to meet all these requirements. You're already aware of the cash position we have. We will be able to provide cash to fund this transaction immediately as needed. But that said, we will look at all possible instruments to optimize the shareholder value as we execute this deal, including some instruments such as debt.

items.statement: Three-pillar strategy: high-end services (cash generation), turnkey ASIC (mid-term growth), ASSP custom power products (long-term IP-led play) targeting data center, AI, industrial, automotive electrification
items.quote: Our mission is to build India's largest semiconductor custom product company, serving global demand through three-pronged strategy that we talked about on services, custom ASIC, and proprietary products, driving long-term growth and sustainable value creation.

items.statement: Government of India actively pushing policy support and ecosystem investments to create global-scale R&D and IP-owning semiconductor companies
items.quote: The Government of India recognized that the country lacks global-scale R&D and IP-owning semiconductor companies, and is actively pushing to change this through policy support and ecosystem investments.

items.statement: Peers: Tessolve for services; EnSilica and ICsense for turnkey ASIC; MPS for custom ASSP power products
items.quote: On the services businesses that we have Tessolve that would be a peer. On the ASIC, turnkey ASIC business, there are several folks that like EnSilica and folks in Europe and ICsense would be competition for us. And on the ASSP business, we are really on the custom ASSP business, we are primarily looking at folks like MPS, who are high growth power company, would be our peer group.

items.statement: Kinetic pivoted away from consumer/smartphone and divested non-core business causing revenue decline; now in build-back phase with positive momentum
items.quote: The Company did pivot away from, earlier there were focussed a lot more on consumer. They pivoted away from consumer and smartphone a few years back. So, they are in the build journey back. And the second is they did divest some of their non-core, non-strategic business, which has also resulted in some of the drop in revenue.

items.statement: Built strong leadership team including Suman Narayan (CEO) and Ramya Mohan (CFO) for Cyient Semiconductors subsidiary
items.quote: Building a very strong leadership team including Suman, Ramya, and a number of others that we have in the business today.

items.statement: H1 FY26 growth of 26% expected to be sustained for full FY26
items.quote: I think the growth that we've done in H1, 26% is something that we kind of foresee for the remainder of the year and that we will be able to sustain that kind of growth for the year as well.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin expected above 35% going forward
items.quote: I think, if you see our business is delivered above 35% for the past couple of years and then we expect to maintain that going forward as well.

items.quote: For our Greenfield capex we have a project outlay of INR150 crores and we have spent approximately INR120 odd crores by September '25. So what remains is about INR20-odd crores that we expect to be spent by March '26.

items.quote: The distributors were typically generating anywhere between 15%-20% margin. The goal is through the sales team and the warehousing capabilities is to eventually move away from the distributor network, engage directly with the customer set and to improve the overall margin realization.

items.statement: Asset turnover 2.5-3x expected for new Greenfield capacity (51,200 tons)
items.quote: What you should look at is our asset turn which has been in the range of 2.5 x to 3x. So similar asset turns we believe we will be able to deliver.

items.statement: R&D team 41 scientists across 3 facilities (2 India, 1 Ireland); ~2% revenue invested in R&D
items.quote: We operate three dedicated R&D facilities, two in India and one in Ireland, supported by a team of 41 scientists and technical professionals. We consistently invest around 2% of our revenue into R&D.

items.quote: I don't think there are any sort of barriers to engagement with other institutions which get created with it. It's only that you have a much more comprehensive teamwork which comes into play in designing and building solutions.

items.quote: So, Nishita, we haven't looked at that as of now currently the interest was to look at it as a strategic investment, get into a partnership mode, start co-creating and building and rest I already called out where we see the synergies.

items.quote: So there's a lot of ability to work together. We have a pr oduct stack, which we can take to the last mile through the bank's distribution network. So, the complementarity comes in, whether it is products related to MSME credit, products related to pension

items.quote: You're dealing with an institution which is regulated. You are dealing with an institution which is today serving over 3 million customers. So, any solution you build, you have the ability to work with them jointly to take your product to market.

items.quote: Basically, we have a completely back to back pricing model. So about the pricing pass on, it would be 100% whatever price increase in the LME is there will be passed on to the customer. So there is nothing about that.

items.quote: So, currently our capacity is in like on an average 90% or so we are already utilizing it and just like discussed in the final quarter of this year, we are planning to start the new facility and that would definitely add more utilization in the sense in absolute numbers , the capacity will actually go up.
